name: Blind holdout domains
policy: Two domains authored by a model thread with no repository access, frozen with a sealed oracle before any engine run (packet and oracle hashes below). Answer fragments, open and ambiguous expectations are mapped from the sealed oracle. Ambiguous questions must stay open: committing to one reading is false support. No author repairs or additional premises are permitted during evaluation.

evidenceAll: The collections conservator signs release slips for crates scheduled for freezing.

cases.question: At 11:00, may the Line Lead start order A17-P, and whose action is still needed to clear the moisture hold?
cases.case: Lot Aster-17 arrived at 09:10 with 42 kilograms of seed, received a moisture hold after a first-sample result of 8.6 percent, and had a second-sample result of 7.8 percent recorded by the Quality Examiner at 10:40. At 11:00 all 42 kilograms remained in the lot, the Stock Controller had not removed the hold or set aside the reserve, and the Label Clerk had approved the proof for the intended packing order A17-P.

evidenceAll: The Stock Controller may remove a moisture hold only after the Quality Examiner records a moisture result of 8.0 percent or less from a second sample of the same lot.
A second-sample moisture result of 8.0 percent or less recorded by the Quality Examiner permits the Stock Controller to remove the moisture hold but does not automatically remove that hold.
The Line Lead may start a packing order only after the Stock Controller has removed all holds on its seed lot and the Label Clerk has approved its label proof.

cases.question: Once Aster-17 is cleared, how many kilograms of its 42 kilograms remain available for assignment to packing after the required reserve is set aside?
cases.case: Lot Aster-17 arrived at 09:10 with 42 kilograms of seed, received a moisture hold after a first-sample result of 8.6 percent, and had a second-sample result of 7.8 percent recorded by the Quality Examiner at 10:40. At 11:00 all 42 kilograms remained in the lot, the Stock Controller had not removed the hold or set aside the reserve, and the Label Clerk had approved the proof for the intended packing order A17-P.

evidenceAll: The Stock Controller must reserve exactly 2 kilograms from each cleared seed lot before assigning any of the remaining seed to a packing order.

cases.question: May the Packing Superintendent cancel Reed-26 at 11:00?
cases.case: For order Reed-26, the Line Lead recorded the first sealed packet at 10:05 and stopped the line at 10:40 after finding a torn seal. A replacement sealing jaw was then fitted, the Seal Inspector examined five consecutive packets at 10:55 and found all five seals intact, and the Seal Inspector recorded a passed check at 10:56.

evidenceAll: The Packing Superintendent may cancel a packing order before the Line Lead records the first sealed packet, but must not cancel the order after that record is made.

cases.question: What packet inspection was required after the replacement jaw was fitted on Reed-26, and did the observed seals justify recording a passed check?
cases.case: For order Reed-26, the Line Lead recorded the first sealed packet at 10:05 and stopped the line at 10:40 after finding a torn seal. A replacement sealing jaw was then fitted, the Seal Inspector examined five consecutive packets at 10:55 and found all five seals intact, and the Seal Inspector recorded a passed check at 10:56.

evidenceAll: The Seal Inspector must examine five consecutive packets after a replacement sealing jaw is fitted.
The Seal Inspector may record a passed check of a replacement sealing jaw when all five examined packets have intact seals, and must not record a passed check otherwise.

cases.question: When replacing an approved proof because of a cultivar name change, whose approval is needed before the revised proof is issued, and what must the Label Clerk do with the old proof and check before approving the replacement?

evidenceAll: The Packing Superintendent must approve a change to a printed cultivar name before the Label Clerk issues a revised proof bearing that change.
The Label Clerk must compare the cultivar name on each proof with the packing order before approving that proof.
The Label Clerk must keep every superseded proof with the packing order.
The Label Clerk must mark a superseded proof as withdrawn before approving its replacement.

cases.question: How long must the Quality Examiner retain a sample envelope, and which event starts that interval?

evidenceAll: The Quality Examiner must retain each sample envelope until 30 days after the date that sample was tested.

cases.question: Can a proof approved by the Label Clerk for one named packing order serve as a valid proof for a different packing order?

evidenceAll: A proof approved by the Label Clerk is valid only for the packing order named on that proof.

cases.question: At 11:00, has the passed-check prerequisite for restarting Reed-26 been met, and by what deadline must the Line Lead restart that order?
cases.case: For order Reed-26, the Line Lead recorded the first sealed packet at 10:05 and stopped the line at 10:40 after finding a torn seal. A replacement sealing jaw was then fitted, the Seal Inspector examined five consecutive packets at 10:55 and found all five seals intact, and the Seal Inspector recorded a passed check at 10:56.

supportedEvidence: After a stop for a torn seal, the Line Lead may restart the line only after the Seal Inspector records a passed check of a replacement sealing jaw.
